observations: col_left L12: «Schöner» has the diaeresis on the o.

col_left L16: a small slanting stroke (1.0 by 1.2 points) over the V of «{sc:xxvii}», 7.1–8.3 points above the baseline, is not transcribed. The lower left foot of the second X of «{sc:xxv}» stands apart like a point; it is not a point.
col_left L18: the t of the second «sciothericum» is printed without its crossbar, like l; read t.

col_left L20: the t of «et» runs into a point under the baseline (1.4 points wide at the baseline, ending 1.1 points below it): a spur of the letter, not the dot of ṭ, which on these pages is round, 1.2–1.6 points across, and ends 1.4–1.7 points below the baseline (as under the t of Sibṭ in L21 of the right column), measured at 8,000 dpi; read t.
col_left L23, L26: «Sédillot» has the acute on the e.
col_left L24: specks (0.6 by 0.5 and 0.6 by 0.7 point) on the baseline before «154» and before «160» are not transcribed; the points of this type are 1.6–2.0 points across.

col_left L25: the point after «em» of «(em.)» is printed with a smear running down to the right (1.8 by 2.3 points, its foot 0.8 point below the baseline), read at 8,000 dpi: the tails of the commas of this type turn to the left (as after «n» in L36); read as a point.
col_left L26: «342»: the upper and the lower ball of the 3 stand apart, like a colon before it; read 342.
col_left L30: the e of the second «diametrus» is printed broken, its loop open; read e.

col_left L31: «semidifferentia» is printed with the ff ligature; the e after it is printed broken; read e. A speck (0.8 by 0.8 point) on the baseline after «duorum» is not transcribed. The d of «dierum» is printed broken, its bowl apart from the stem; read d.
col_left L32: «*semuz*» is printed in italics.

col_left L33: the n of «Send» is printed broken, the middle of its arch missing, read at 8,000 dpi; its left stem has the foot serif of an n, not the bowl of a u; read Send. «‘Alī» begins with the sign of ‘ayn and has the bar over the i.

col_left L35: «Shakakō» has the bar over the o and «Shakkū» over the u. Under the second k of «Shakakō» a short spur (0.7 point wide, ending 0.7 point below the baseline) hangs from the letter, read at 8,000 dpi; it is not the dot of a letter with a dot below (those are 1.2–1.6 points across); read k.

col_left L36: «n, 7;» is printed with a comma after the n (a head with a tail turning left, 1.8 by 2.4 points, its foot 0.9 point below the baseline), where the index has a point; transcribed as printed. After the point of «i.» a thin slanting stroke (0.7 by 1.3 points), from the baseline to 1 point below it, like the tail of a comma without its head, is not transcribed. A speck (0.7 by 1.0 point) under the c of «Iacobus» is not transcribed; it is not a cedilla.
col_left L38: the l of «sextilis» (the first word) is printed with a hook running below the baseline (0.8 point), like J; read l.
col_left L39: the i of «lin.» has a thin spur running 1.9 points below the baseline (0.4 point wide at its end); read i.
col_left L40: the o of «supputatio» is printed broken, open at the top, like υ; read o.
col_left L41: «Shādhān» has the bars over both a (touching the letters) and «Baḥr» the dot under the h.
col_left L42: «Shāfi‘itarum» has the bar over the a, the fi ligature (the a and the f run together) and the sign of ‘ayn.
col_left L44: «*ash-Shāh*» is printed in italics, with the bar over the a.

col_left L45: «ash-Shahrastānī» has the bars over the a and the last i (2.0 by 0.8 points). Small spurs hang under the a after the r (0.9 point wide, ending 0.75 point below the baseline) and under the middle of the first X of «{sc:xxx}» (1.0 point wide, ending 1.0 point below it), read at 8,000 dpi; neither is a dot below.

col_left L46: «ash-Shahrazūrī» has the bars over the u and the last i; «Muḥ.» and «Maḥmūd» have the dots under the h, read at 3,000 dpi; «Maḥmūd» has the bar over the u. The left foot of the M of «Muḥ.» stands apart, and the d of «Maḥmūd» is printed broken (like ‹(l›); read d.
col_right L1: «*ash-shakl al-qaṭṭā‘*» is printed in italics, with the dots under both t, the bar over the a and the sign of ‘ayn at the end.
col_right L2: «*shama‘ī*» is printed in italics, with the sign of ‘ayn and the bar over the i.

col_right L3: «ash-Shammākhī» has the bars over the a and the last i; «Abū» the bar over the u; «’l-‘Abbās» the apostrophe of elision, the sign of ‘ayn and the bar over the second a; «Aḥmad» the dot under the h; «Sa‘īd» the sign of ‘ayn and the bar over the i (1.9 by 1.1 points).
col_right L4: «‘Abd» begins with the sign of ‘ayn; «al-Wāḥid» has the bar over the a, the dot under the h and a round dot on the i.

col_right L5: a small comma-shaped speck (0.8 by 1.7 points), from 0.8 point above to 0.9 point below the baseline, 1.9 points after «Shams», is not transcribed: the commas of this type are 1.6–1.9 points wide and 2.2–3.5 points tall. «ad-dīn» has the bar over the i and «al-Bukhārī» the bars over the a and the last i.

col_right L6: the lower feet of several small capitals (the X of «{sc:xxxvii}», the L of «{sc:lxxiv}») stand apart like points; none is a point. A speck under the first X of «{sc:xxxi}» is not transcribed.

col_right L8: «*ash-sharaṭāni*» is printed in italics, with the dot under the t, the bar over the a and a round dot on the last i. A speck (0.7 by 0.7 point) under the first h, 0.3–1.0 point below the baseline, is not transcribed; the dots below of the italic are 1.1–1.7 points across.
col_right L9: «ash-Sharqī» has the bar over the i; «‘Alī» the sign of ‘ayn and a short bar over the i (1.6 by 0.7 points); «Aḥmad» the dot under the h.

col_right L11: «*shibbūr*» is printed in italics, with the bar over the u. The Hebrew «שׁבור» is printed without vowel points, read at 8,000 dpi: shin with its dot at the upper right, bet without dagesh, vav, resh; the short vertical stroke under the shin belongs to the letter. A round blot (2.3 by 2.5 points) about 75 points after the end of the line is not transcribed.
col_right L12: «*ash-shi‘rà ash-sha’miyyah*» is printed in italics, with the sign of ‘ayn, the grave on the a of «shi‘rà» and the apostrophe of the hamzah; «α» is Greek.
col_right L13: «=» is printed as a long equals sign. «al-ghumayṣā’» has the dot under the s, the bar over the a and the apostrophe of the hamzah.
col_right L15: «*ash-shi‘rà al-yamāniyyah*» is printed in italics, with the sign of ‘ayn, the grave on the a of «shi‘rà» and the bar over the second a.

col_right L16: «*Shû-king*» is printed in italics, with the circumflex on the u (its right arm joined to the letter), read at 6,000 dpi. A speck (0.5 by 0.7 point) on the baseline before «272» is not transcribed.
col_right L18: «Shu‘ūbiyyah» has the sign of ‘ayn and the bar over the second u.
col_right L19: «al-Battānī» has the bars over the second a and the last i; both i of «iis» have their dots (the first one small).
col_right L20: the first i of «Sībawayhi» has a short bar (1.7 by 1.0 points), flatter than the round dot of its last i (1.6 by 1.4 points), read at 3,000 dpi; transcribed as printed.

col_right L21: «Sibṭ» (twice) has the dot under the t; «al-Māridīnī» has the bar over the a, a round dot on the first i (1.3 by 1.3 points) and the bars over the second and the last i; the left foot of its M stands apart. «Muḥ.» has the dot under the h. «Sibṭ. . . . .» is printed with five points after the t, 4.0–4.7 points apart, the first 2.7 points after the letter (as «Iabet. . . . .,» on p. 396).
col_right L23: «*Siddhānta-Śiromaṇi*» is printed in italics, with the bar over the a, the acute on the S and the dot under the n; «Bhāskara» has the bar over the a.
col_right L26: «significantes» is printed with the fi ligature. A speck (0.8 by 0.8 point) under the m of «hebdomadae» is not transcribed.

col_right L29: the comma after «II» is printed short (1.7 by 2.2 points, its foot 0.7 point below the baseline); a round speck (1.0 by 0.7 point) on the baseline after it is not transcribed. A speck (0.8 point across, ending 1.1 points below the baseline) under the t of «et» is not transcribed; it is smaller than the dots of ṭ.

col_right L35, L38: «1°» (twice) is printed with the same small raised o as the degree sign of «90°» on p. 404 (compared at 8,000 dpi) and transcribed with it. «Dhū ’l-qarnayn» has the bar over the u and the apostrophe of elision.

col_right L39: under the second d of «add.» a spur hangs from the bowl (1.6 points wide at the baseline, tapering to a point 1.1 points below it): not the dot of ḍ, which is round, 1.2–1.4 points across, and ends 1.4–1.7 points below the baseline («Riḍwān», pp. 403 and 404), measured at 8,000 dpi; read d.
col_right L41: «fixa» is printed with the fi ligature.
col_right L42: «*murtabiṭah*» is printed in italics, with the dot under the t.

col_right L44: «*as-simāk al-a‘zal*» is printed in italics, with the bar over the a and the sign of ‘ayn; the c and the a of «Spica» run together, the ball of the c standing apart; read Spica. «α» is Greek.
col_right L46: «*as-simāk ar-rāmiḥ*» is printed in italics, with the bars over both a and the dot under the h; «α» is Greek.

col_right L22: the closing parenthesis of «{sc:xxx})» is printed broken: its lower end (1.6 by 2.3 points, from 0.2 to 2.5 points below the baseline) stands apart, like a comma before the point; read ).
col_right L28: the t of «et» is printed without its crossbar, like l; read t. A speck (0.4 by 0.6 point) under the first m of «mensium» is not transcribed.
col_right L33: a speck (0.6 by 0.6 point) under the last m of «Persarum», 0.8–1.4 points below the baseline, is not transcribed.

col_right L34: a speck (0.7 by 0.6 point) under the a and the d of «(adn.», 1.1–1.7 points below the baseline, is not transcribed; it is not a dot below (those of this type are 1.2–1.6 points across and hang from their letters).
col_right L35: a speck (0.7 by 0.8 point) under the e and the p of «septembris», 0.7–1.5 points below the baseline, is not transcribed.
col_right L46: the B of «Bootis» is printed broken, its stem apart from its bowls (like ‹Iʒ›); the first o is open at the top, like υ, and the t has no crossbar; read Bootis.

col_left, col_right: specks of 0.5–1.2 points (the points of this type are 1.5–2.0 points across) on and under the baseline in the margins, before L9, L17, L35, L36, L38–L40 and L44 of the left column and L4, L21, L28, L29 and L43 of the right, and after the ends of L15, L20, L25, L28, L30, L32, L33, L36, L37, L43 and L45 of the left column and L16, L20 and L24 of the right (the largest, 1.0–1.2 points, 9–21 points after «‘Alī.», «Bartelensis.», «gradus.» and «272.»), are not transcribed.

col_left, col_right: on this page the ball terminals of the 3s often stand apart from the figure, the upper ball at mid height and the lower ball on the baseline, like a colon before the figure (for example in «301», «306», «316» and «327» of L1 and in «153», «234», «235», «237», «324», «330», «342», «293», «303», «314» and «316»); the balls of the 2s, 5s and 9s and of a, r and s often stand apart too. loose_pieces.py lists 195 loose pieces on this page, 62 of them low on the line like points and 61 at mid height; none of them is a point.
